resolutions.researcher_notes: COULD NOT SOURCE THE RECORDED VALUE (StartYear1=2022) — and what I found actively disagrees with it, not just by rounding. EIA's 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' tab (EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects.xlsx, already staged on this row for Capacity/Fuel/Length/Operator/SegmentCost/Status) carries this exact project by name — 'Bluewater Compressor Project', operator 'Bluewater Gas Storage', docket CP19-471, notes 'New compressor station to expand capacity from pressure limited 120,000 Mcf/d, to 500,000 Mcf/d on its interconnect with the Vector Pipeline' — and states Status=Completed, Completed Date=2021-11-19, Year In Service Date=2021. That is a full year earlier than the sheet's recorded StartYear1=2022, not a rounding-tolerance gap. The other already-staged doc on this row, Gas Compression Magazine's 2020-02-14 piece (archived), independently corroborates the schedule that produced that 2021 date: Bluewater 'must commence construction of the project facilities by June 2020 for the project to be placed into service prior to the 2021/2022 storage withdrawal season' (which opens ~Nov. 1) — consistent with EIA's Nov. 19, 2021 completion, not with an in-service year of 2022. Both sources name this exact project and agree with each other; neither supports 2022. Also checked the Enbridge factsheet, Wikipedia's Vector_Pipeline page, and offshore-technology.com (all already on this row for __VALIDITY__) — none states a start/in-service year for this specific compressor project. Not forcing this to REFS_ADDED against the recorded value — flagging as a likely sheet error for the orchestrator/human to review (StartYear1 probably belongs at 2021, per EIA's Completed Date of 2021-11-19).

My working read: the 'Delayed=yes/inferred' flag on this row is very likely a downstream artifact of the StartYear1 discrepancy flagged on the Start [ref] record above (the sheet's own recorded StartYear1=2022 sits a year after the sourced actual completion, which may be what GEM's dormancy-inference rule keyed on), rather than a real-world delay to the project. resolutions.researcher_notes: StartState/Province=Michigan, StartCountryOrArea=United States is SOLIDLY confirmed at high tier by two independent, project-named sources: EIA's Historical Projects tab (State=MI) and Gas Compression Magazine's 2020 article ('Macomb County, Michigan, USA'). EndState/Province=Wisconsin, EndCountryOrArea=United States could NOT be confirmed as a literal pipeline terminus — no source (including the FERC-derived EIA record, which lists this as a single-state MI project with no cross-state segment) states a Wisconsin endpoint for the Blue Water Compressor Project specifically, which is a point facility (a compressor station tying into Bluewater's existing 20-inch header in Macomb Co., MI), not a linear MI-to-WI route. What I found instead is an indirect corporate/service-territory link: Bluewater Gas Storage is a WEC Energy Group subsidiary alongside We Energies and Wisconsin Public Service, and Bluewater's own site states it provides seasonal storage for customers of those two Wisconsin-headquartered utilities. That may be why GEM recorded an End=Wisconsin (service territory / corporate family), but it is not the same claim as a physical route endpoint, so tier is medium overall (high for Start, low/indirect for End) rather than high across the whole unit. Flagging the End value for the orchestrator to confirm GEM's intended semantics here (service area vs. route terminus) rather than treating it as settled.
